claims.text: Plasma cladding a WC-reinforced composite surface layer onto a titanium alloy will increase surface hardness relative to the untreated alloy.
Plasma cladding a WC-reinforced composite surface layer onto a titanium alloy will increase wear resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
The untreated conventional titanium alloy has a relatively soft and ductile surface microstructure lacking hard, wear-resistant phases.
A plasma-cladded metallic matrix can incorporate well-dispersed WC particles on a titanium-alloy surface.
The proposed WC-containing matrix will bond strongly to the titanium-alloy substrate.
The coating will improve performance under both dry and lubricated sliding wear at moderate speeds and loads.
WC particles in the surface layer will limit grain growth through a nailing effect and promote a fine-grained metallic matrix.
Anchored WC particles act as barriers to abrasive and adhesive wear.
WC has very high intrinsic hardness.
Hard WC particles resist penetration and deformation during sliding wear.
WC particles diminish microcrack propagation and thereby reduce abrasive material removal.
The metallic matrix spreads applied loads and maintains coating integrity.
The coating will increase surface hardness by at least 50% relative to untreated titanium alloy.
The coating will reduce wear rate by at least 50% relative to untreated titanium alloy under identical sliding conditions.
The beneficial effect will be confined to the engineered surface layer.
High-temperature exposure or severe corrosive environments may delaminate the coating and eliminate the improvement.
Insufficient coating thickness may prevent the improvement from persisting.
The magnitude of hardness and wear improvement depends on WC loading, plasma-cladding parameters, and test conditions.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least 50% improvements, whereas falsification occurs only below 30%. Thus, an outcome between 30% and 49% would fail the stated prediction but would not falsify the hypothesis.
